title: Generalizations of Wilsons Theorem to Non-Prime Moduli

problemStatement.formal: For n ≥ 3: ∏ x : (ZMod n)ˣ, (x : ZMod n) = -1 ↔ IsCyclic (ZMod n)ˣ. The Gauss-Wilson theorem: product of units mod n equals -1 iff the unit group is cyclic, iff n ∈ {4, p^k, 2p^k} for odd prime p.
problemStatement.plain: Prove the Gauss-Wilson theorem abstractly: the product of all units modulo n equals -1 if and only if the unit group (ZMod n)ˣ is cyclic. Build the bridge to the concrete product computation.
whyMatters: Gauss-Wilson theorem is a fundamental generalization of Wilson's theorem
Connects group structure (cyclicity) to arithmetic (unit products)
Provides foundation for primitive root theory in Lean

proven: (∏ x)² = 1 in any finite commutative group (prod_univ_sq_eq_one)
open: Cyclic group even order ⟹ product ≠ 1 (generator argument)
knownResults.goal: Eliminate all sorries: prove the involution lemma, cyclic/non-cyclic product theorems, and concrete-abstract bridge

currentState.nextAction: Prove involution product lemma using Finset.prod_bij. Then use generator to show product ≠ 1 in cyclic groups of even order.

approaches.name: Involution + self-inverse decomposition
approaches.description: Decompose ∏ G into ∏ {self-inverse} via involution pairing. In cyclic group, self-inverse = {1, -1}. Product = -1.

approaches.name: Generator sum approach (alternative for cyclic case)
approaches.description: In cyclic group of order m with generator g: ∏ G = g^(m(m-1)/2). For even m, this equals g^(m/2) = -1.
